companyDescription: Launch + lunar + defense · Alpha rocket + Blue Ghost lunar lander + SciTec (space domain awareness) · $1.3B backlog, 80% of FY26 revenue already booked · Q2 earnings Aug 11, 2026
priceNote: Live-prices.json cache — up 6.58% today as part of a broad tech/semis rally (AMD +7%, AVGO +6.6%, INTC +10.8%, MU +7.6%) rather than FLY-specific news. Still 74-96% below analyst consensus targets even after the bounce, with Q2 earnings landing in 6 days (Aug 11).
summary: Firefly's Q2 2026 earnings date is now confirmed for Aug 11, six days out, with FY26 guidance ($420-450M, 80% pre-booked via a $1.3B backlog) still standing from the Q1 print. The stock has traded in an extremely wide $16.00-$73.80 52-week range and jumped 6.58% today in a broad tech/semis rally rather than on FLY-specific news, leaving a wide gap to a 12-analyst MarketBeat consensus target of $40.64 (~74% upside, high $60). Shares outstanding have swelled 710% YoY to 164.24M post-IPO and post-SciTec, pushing market cap to $3.83B on a roughly flat price since mid-July — dilution risk is now a concrete, quantified concern rather than a forward worry, and the Aug 11 print lands one day before the market's own highest-conviction swing event (Aug 12 CPI).

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Reports Tuesday, Aug 11, 2026 — exact date confirmed via a Jul 15 press release. FY26 guidance ($420-450M revenue, 80% pre-booked via backlog) should still hold; the print is mainly about execution/margin trajectory. Lands one day ahead of the market's Aug 12 CPI print, which the site's own market-timing model flags as the key swing event this cycle — implied move ±15-25% for a small-cap like FLY.

catalysts.name: Alpha Block 2 Debut
catalysts.description: Upgraded Alpha rocket configuration — enhanced reliability, increased height, expanded capabilities — still targeted for 'late summer 2026' per the most recent reporting; no confirmed launch as of Aug 5. This is the vehicle upgrade that de-risks Firefly's core launch business after prior Alpha mishaps.

catalysts.name: Blue Ghost 2 Lunar Mission
catalysts.description: Follow-up to Blue Ghost 1's successful Mar 2025 Moon landing (first commercial firm to do so), still targeted for late 2026. Separately, Firefly won a new $144M NASA CLPS contract (Jun 30) for an accelerated future Blue Ghost mission targeted for 2028 — a longer-dated backlog add beyond this cycle.

risks: Alpha's mishap history is real, and Block 2's debut — still undated ('late summer', no confirmed launch as of Aug 5) — is the actual de-risking proof point; a repeat failure would hit the stock hard and delay the narrative further

Extreme realized volatility: FLY has swung across a 52-week range of $16.00-$73.80, including single-day moves of +17.8% (Jun 11), -19.1% (Jun 12), and -13.8% (May 28) — genuinely high-beta even for a space-launch small-cap

Heavy dilution: shares outstanding are up 710% YoY to 164.24M (post-IPO plus the stock-funded SciTec deal), pushing market cap to $3.83B even though price is roughly flat since mid-July — further issuance risk remains live

Dense event cluster right after earnings: the Aug 11 print sits one day before the Aug 12 CPI release the broader market-timing model flags as the key swing event this cycle — a hot CPI surprise could overwhelm even a clean FLY result

Analyst target dispersion remains real: MarketBeat consensus $40.64 (12 analysts, high $60/low $25) vs. stockanalysis.com's $45.80 (10 analysts) — different vintages/coverage sets give meaningfully different upside math

estimateDates.note: 80% of FY26 guide already booked — print is about execution, not demand; lands one day before market-wide Aug 12 CPI
De-risks the core launch business after last year's mishaps; still no confirmed launch as of Aug 5

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed held at 3.50-3.75% at the Jul 29 FOMC, but 3 voting members dissented in favor of a hike — an unusual hawkish split. Next FOMC is Sep 15-16, 2026. Small-cap high-beta names like FLY stay more exposed to a higher-for-longer repricing than the broad market.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core PCE is still running 3.3% YoY (Jun), well above the 2% target. The Aug 12 CPI print — one day after FLY's own Aug 11 earnings — is the market's key swing event this cycle.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: MEDIUM-HIGH — S&P 500 is near record highs (crossed 7,600) with broadening breadth (~65-70% of stocks above 50DMA) and a calm VIX (~15.8), but HY credit spreads are historically tight (~281bps vs. ~450bps long-run median) — a 'priced to perfection' setup. FLY's own earnings land directly inside the Aug 7 NFP → Aug 12 CPI risk window.
macroRisk.summary: Fed risk MEDIUM for FLY specifically — broad market technicals are constructive (record highs, improving breadth), but FLY's Aug 11 earnings sits one day before the market's highest-conviction swing event (Aug 12 CPI) against a backdrop where the Fed just saw a hawkish 3-member dissent. A clean Q2 print could still get overwhelmed by a hot CPI surprise the next day.

Same-sector precedent for how quickly space-launch gains can evaporate on sector-wide sentiment even after strong fundamentals — directly relevant given FLY's own extreme realized volatility this year.

macroRisk.summary: ความเสี่ยง Fed ระดับปานกลางเฉพาะหุ้นนี้ — technical ตลาดรวมดี (จุดสูงสุด, breadth กว้างขึ้น) แต่ earnings 11 ส.ค. ของ FLY อยู่ก่อนหน้า event ชี้ขาดของตลาด (CPI 12 ส.ค.) แค่ 1 วัน ท่ามกลาง Fed ที่เพิ่งมี hawkish dissent 3 เสียง ผล Q2 ที่ดีอาจโดนกลบด้วย CPI ร้อนแรงวันถัดไปได้
